doc.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Many stars, not one: against the single-narrative history
summary: Brower and Fuller say jazz history wants a single star, while Fuller sees thousands of stars.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well that’s… Well, there is a need, where there seems to be a need for a simple narrative that explains everything. We live in a star system so they only make one room for one start. We have sat here and we've been discussing trombone players up ying yang. You can do that and we have gone from city, to city, to city and identified cats as killer.

I’m gladly while it up at the heavens I see thousands of the stars. They light up my world. I don’t think one star could do that. It may be good for a seamen, “Oh, there’s the north star, I think I’ll follow that.” I’m talking about in general.
We sort of live on the notion of impoverishment. Like, there can only be a few great things.
